Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in fitness & wellness. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

Gym and studio management software

Holds members, plans, classes, bookings and attendance. We read and write through the vendor's API or exports, and keep plan rules in the software rather than duplicating them elsewhere.

  • FitnessForce
  • Glofox
  • Wellyx
  • Mindbody
  • Momence
  • bsport

Salon and spa software

Holds the appointment book, client cards, services, staff skills and POS sales. Booking, reminders, rebooking intervals and commission statements read from here.

  • Zenoti
  • Dingg
  • MioSalon
  • Invoay
  • Fresha

Access control and check-in

Records who came in and when. Attendance patterns use check-in events only; biometric templates stay in the access system and never enter our workflows.

  • Biometric or face recognition terminals
  • QR code check-in apps
  • RFID card turnstiles
  • Aggregator QR check-in

Coaching and practice platforms

Hold client programs, plans, check-ins and messages for coaches and dietitians. Intake routing, check-in summaries and plan formatting connect here, with the professional's approval step.

  • Practice Better
  • Trainerize
  • Healthie
  • TrueCoach

Payments, mandates and accounting

Collect payments, deposits, installments and recurring debits through hosted links, UPI Autopay and card mandates, and keep the books. Card and UPI credentials stay with the gateway.

  • Razorpay
  • Cashfree
  • PayU
  • Stripe
  • Tally
  • Zoho Books

Aggregators, listings and booking platforms

Where people find, book and review. We work with partner portals, exports and official APIs, respect each platform's terms, and never scrape member data out of partner apps.

  • cultpass
  • Fitpass
  • Google Business Profile
  • Instagram
  • Retreat Guru

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Inquiry first response time

Median time from a new inquiry on WhatsApp, Instagram, Google or a lead form to the first meaningful reply by the system or a person, by channel and hour of day.

Why it matters: People message several gyms, salons or coaches at once, and the first useful reply often wins the trial, appointment or call.

Trial-to-member conversion

Trial or intro-offer visitors who buy a membership, class pack or program within an agreed period, divided by trial visitors who attended, by campaign and consultant.

Why it matters: Shows whether ad spend and free trials turn into paying members, and which follow-ups work.

Class and chair utilization

Attended class places, or booked chair, room and therapist hours, as a share of available capacity, by time slot, location and staff member.

Why it matters: Capacity is perishable; utilization shows where waitlists, reminders and schedules are doing their job.

No-show and late cancellation rate

Bookings not attended or canceled inside the agreed cutoff, divided by all bookings for the class, service or day.

Why it matters: Reminders, waitlists and a consistent policy exist to protect peak slots and long services.

Attendance-drop follow-up

Members flagged for an attendance drop who were contacted by their trainer or teacher within the agreed time, and the share of them who returned within an agreed period.

Why it matters: Tests whether early, personal contact brings drifting members back before the renewal decision.

On-time renewal rate

Plans renewed on or before their end date as a share of plans due in the period, with freezes and cancellations reported separately.

Why it matters: Renewals are the economics of a membership business, and clear notice should raise them without hiding the way out.

Rebooking within the due window

Salon clients who book their next service within an agreed window around their recommended interval, as a share of clients due in the period, by stylist and service.

Why it matters: Regular clients on their natural interval are the most reliable revenue a salon has.

Failed payment recovery

Failed recurring debits or installments paid within an agreed period after failure, as a share of all failed payments in the period.

Why it matters: Most failed debits are accidental; polite, prompt recovery keeps members who never meant to leave.

Check-in review time

Median time from a client's weekly check-in to the coach's reply, plus the share of concern flags reviewed by a qualified professional the same day.

Why it matters: Clients stay with coaches who respond, and concern flags must never wait behind routine messages.

Review reply coverage

Share of new Google reviews with an approved reply, and median time from review to reply, by location.

Why it matters: Thoughtful replies show prospective members and clients that the business listens and fixes problems.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
